title: [finding] Four cards in one night share one shape: a factual claim written in prose that no instrument can read — and for half of them there is no anchor for one to read
body:
Filed by the triage seat, `date -u` measured 2026-09-09T11:28Z, on `origin/main` `50b6f17d`. ⛔ Filed on a **pre-registered trigger**, not on a hunch: this seat recorded the pattern at its third instance (#16954, 2026-09-09T07:28Z) with the words 「⛔ 未测这是否构成一个值得统一处置的族;若第四次出现,值得立一张族卡」. The fourth arrived (#16940). This is that card.

⚠️ The reason for pre-registering rather than filing at instance three is on the record: this repo has already been bitten by a trigger that fired and was not acted on — **#15189**'s own note 「以便第三次发生时有据可查」 had, when triage read it, fired **six times over**.

## The shape

> A factual claim is written in prose. Nothing mechanical can notice when it becomes false. It is found only by a hand sweep for the claim's **own tokens** — and by then it has usually been wrong for a while, or has been copied.

## The four instances, each with its measured instrument-blindness

| # | the claim | why no instrument reads it |
|---|---|---|
| **#17065** | `path:NNN` anchors inside `packages/spec/src/**` docblocks | ⭐ A shared resolver EXISTS (`scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`) and corpora join it by `defineCorpus`. Three are registered (`docs/adr/**`, `scripts/**`, the system-context page). Spec docblocks are simply **not registered** |
| **#16850** | a card's named `.changeset/*.md` path, as a deliverable | nothing watches for a release **consuming** that file; two cards silently blew the deadline |
| **#16954** | the route-census figures `22/30`, `73%` | the stale carrier spells the call `register(` and never says `80` ⇒ **invisible to every query the repairing card was scoped by**; only a sweep for the FIGURES found it |
| **#16940** | «the batch cap is the deployment's, configurable 1–1000» | the page states the rule **by its inputs** (a value, a range, an error code) and shares no identifier with the emitter, whose carrier is a **private** method ⇒ `affected-docs.mjs` reports it in neither list. Its filer's own words: *"a tool-reported 0 for pages of this shape is **not a clean bill**"* |

## ⭐ The split that makes this actionable — and that no single card above could see

The four are **not one problem**. They divide cleanly, and the division decides whether a gate is even possible:

**(A) Anchored — an identifier exists, nothing reads it.** #17065. Here a mechanism is already built and ruled: the 2026-09-01 ruling on #13556 says a corpus joins by registration, 「共享同一个 resolver,⛔ 不造第二套」. ⇒ Tractable, and #17065 already owns it. ⛔ This card does not duplicate it.

**(B) Unanchored — there is no identifier for any resolver to resolve.** #16954 and #16940. A figure (`73%`) and a restated rule (`configurable 1–1000`) contain nothing that ties them to their source. ⇒ **A symbol-anchor gate cannot help**, and the honest question is whether anything mechanical can.

**(C) Lifecycle — the claim is fine, its referent is consumed.** #16850. A different mechanism again (watch the artefact, not the text).

⇒ ⭐ **The load-bearing question this card exists to answer is (B), and it may well be "no gate — a discipline".** That is a legitimate answer and should be reachable without anyone feeling they failed to build something.

## What is asked — ⛔ first deliverable is the decision, NOT a gate

1. **Rule whether (B) is mechanically readable at all.** If a claim carries no identifier, the candidates are all expensive and lossy (semantic diffing of prose against source; a required "claims this restates X" annotation on restating passages; nothing).
2. **If the answer is "no gate": say so, and write down the discipline instead** — the one all four filers actually used and that worked: ⭐ **when repairing a claim, sweep for the claim's own FIGURES and TOKENS, not for the identifier or the sentence shape.** #16954's repair missed a carrier precisely by sweeping the sentence family; #16940 was found only by a token sweep. That sentence, written where a repairer reads it, is cheap and is the measured remedy.
3. ⛔ **Do not fold (A) or (C) in.** #17065 and #16850 own those and are tractable on their own terms; merging would stall two solvable cards behind an open question.

## ⚠️ What is NOT claimed

- ⛔ **No population count.** This card names four instances found in one night's triage of ONE page of one repo's backlog. ⚠️ That is a lower bound on a biased sample, ⛔ **not a rate and not a census**. Whoever takes it should take a real count before sizing any remedy.
- ⛔ Not that the four cards are duplicates of each other — they are not, and each should land on its own.
- ⛔ Not a proposal to build anything. Option "nothing, plus a written discipline" is explicitly on the table and may be right.
- ⚠️ Not measured: whether `objectui` has the same class. Only `objectstack` was swept.

## Re-grade trigger (written hard, so this one is not another #15189)

- A **fifth** instance of class (B) ⇒ **p2**, and the population count becomes urgent rather than first-deliverable.
- Any instance of (B) that is measured to have **misled a change** (not merely been stale) ⇒ **p2**.

## Lane note

`domain:devx`: the deliverables are a `scripts/`-side judgement and, most likely, a line of written discipline about repair method — the devx row's 「治理代码/文档质量」. ⚠️ ⛔ Not `domain:skills`: the skills row takes only `.claude/skills/**`, `skills/**`, the root constitution files, and gates whose SUBJECT is the **governed surface itself** (currently only `scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs`) — a distinction this seat mis-read once today and corrected on #16995, and which #16993 tracks.

Refs: #17065 · #16850 · #16954 · #16940 · #15189 (the registry whose own trigger fired six times unheeded) · #13556 (the shared-resolver ruling) · #16993
